data.description: Existing browser used by uploaders and reviewers; outside provisioning scope. The application authenticates staff and enforces separate upload and reviewer permissions.

data.label: Invoice intake and approval
data.description: Composed invoice-workflow deployment unit on Azure Container Apps, owning browser/API, background worker and isolated PDF/OCR parser. Internal generated resources include Azure Database for PostgreSQL durable queue/outbox and review state, private versioned Azure Blob Storage originals, staff sign-in, separate workload identities, regional model integration and operating tasks/monitoring. Accept PDF invoices up to 10,000,000 bytes; plan for approximately 500 uploads daily, with peak throughput and completion time unspecified. Treat originals and extracted fields as Confidential and potentially personal data. Extract supplier, invoice date, total and currency with source evidence; incomplete or failed extraction stays visible for review. Commit workflow state and queued work transactionally; use bounded retries and recover stalled work. Bind reviewer approval to the exact result revision and delivery payload. Send with a stable operation identity; fence uncertain accounting outcomes for reconciliation rather than blindly resending. Accounting must independently pass normalized-action-v1 and durable idempotency acceptance. Keep documents and extracted data in Australia, including processing, queues, logs containing invoice data, backups and recovery copies. Australia East is proposed, not an approved region decision; verify Container Apps, PostgreSQL, Blob Storage, regional model availability, quotas, private networking and processing geography before destination selection. Do not silently use global or cross-region model processing. Retain originals and extraction audit history for 90 days; qualify cleanup scheduling, object versions, SQL records and backup expiry rather than promise exact universal erasure. Confirm the retention start event during implementation. Keep invoice content out of routine operational logs. Parser isolation, model-service retention/abuse-monitoring policy, restore behavior and operating ownership require qualification. This diagram proves no deployment.

data.label: Existing accounting API
data.description: Client-owned existing accounting service, referenced without recreation or modification. Receives only approved invoice payloads through an authenticated adapter. Native API mapping, durable idempotency, result lookup/reconciliation and permission scope remain unverified; the normalized contract alone does not establish compatibility. Its processing, storage, logging and backup locations are unknown and must be qualified against the Australian residency requirement before transferring extracted invoice data.

REQ-001 — must functional other: Accept uploaded PDF invoices, asynchronously extract supplier, invoice date, total and currency, and persist results in a review queue. Proposed acceptance: show supporting evidence and expose incomplete extraction or processing failures for correction. (open)

REQ-002 — must functional security: Permit accounting submission only after an authorized reviewer approves the exact result revision and delivery payload; changes invalidate that approval. Enforce reviewer permissions on the server and retain the approval and delivery history. (open)

REQ-003 — must nonfunctional reliability: Repeated delivery and worker recovery must not create duplicate accounting invoices. Persist stable operation and payload identities, require a qualified destination idempotency contract, and reconcile uncertain external outcomes before allowing another submission. (open)

REQ-004 — must nonfunctional compliance: Keep invoice documents and extracted data within Australia across application processing, model inference, storage and data-bearing operational/recovery copies. Qualify the existing accounting destination before transfer. Explicitly flag unverified regional service/model support and prohibit silent cross-border fallback. (open)

REQ-005 — must nonfunctional compliance: Retain invoice originals and extraction audit history for 90 days. Implement scheduled cleanup and document deletion behavior for database records, object versions and backups; qualify the retention start event and residual recovery windows before claiming compliance. [Original and extraction-audit retention period == 90days] (open)

REQ-006 — must nonfunctional scalability: Accept PDF invoices up to 10,000,000 bytes and plan asynchronous capacity for approximately 500 uploads per day. Reject oversized uploads explicitly before parsing. Qualify capacity with representative PDFs and retry/recovery workloads; peak arrival rate and completion-time targets remain unspecified. (open)
